newsitem.title: USA: North Carolina governor proposes welfare changes.
newsitem.headline: North Carolina governor proposes welfare changes.

text.p: North Carolina Gov. Jim Hunt said Tuesday he would seek legislation that would freeze counties' welfare spending at fiscal 1997 levels.
The proposal would give counties more control and flexibility over how to spend welfare funds, Hunt said.
But they would be required to keep the same core services, such as providing cash assistance and employment services, and requiring absent parents to pay child support.
They would also be required to cut their welfare rolls, move recipients into the workplace and ensure that they remain in the workplace.
Those who fail to meet the goals would be required to submit plans to the state detailing how they would improve. The state would have the option to take over those that fail to improve.
Savings acheived by trimming the welfare rolls would be used to provide child care subsidies for welfare recipients and those at risk of going on welfare.
Welfare recipients would continue to receive full cash benefits for three months after they get a job, and would continue to receive transportation assistance for six months.

Hunt said he would present the proposal in detail to the General Assembly later this week. He said the changes would strengthen the state's Work First program, which has helped cut welfare rolls by 19.3 percent and saved $90 million since it took effect 20 months ago.
